situation:
You are the shop manager of CITY SPOKE E-BIKES, a two-year-old rental and repair shop three blocks from the riverfront trail. The founder (judge) opened the shop with a single round of investment, and that money runs out in roughly five months. Until now CITY SPOKE E-BIKES has charged for only two things, rentals by the hour and repairs by the job.

The shop promises every customer that a bike left in the morning is back on the road the same day, and that promise is what CITY SPOKE E-BIKES is known for on the trail. The shop has one repair bay and two mechanics, so the promise holds only as long as a day's work fits the bay. On summer weekends the work already does not fit.

Two groups of customers want that bay. Weekend renters, mostly visitors riding the trail, turn up with flat tires and dead batteries and pay by the job at full price. Weekday commuters bring the same bike back every few weeks and want somebody to keep it running for them. The founder (judge) wants to sell those commuters a monthly maintenance membership, the first product the shop has ever had to price.

Priced low, at nineteen dollars a month, the membership sells quickly and fills the bay with member work, which pushes out the walk-in weekend repairs that earn far more per hour. Priced high, at forty-five dollars a month, few commuters sign up, the bay stays open for walk-in repairs, and the steady monthly income the shop needs before the investment runs out may never arrive.

The founder (judge) has asked you to recommend a price for the maintenance membership, and to explain what that price does to demand for the one repair bay and to the same-day promise. The founder (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the founder (judge) of CITY SPOKE E-BIKES. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have five months of money left and you want a monthly maintenance membership on sale before the summer ends. You want the shop manager's recommendation on what to charge for it, and you want to hear what that price does to the repair bay, to the weekend renters and to the commuters.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: If you had recommended the other price, what would it have cost us?
What would that price have done for us that yours does not?
